To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the biohydrogenated fatty acids of stearidionic acid are not the same as those of linolenic or linoleic acids.

the biohydrogenated intermediates of 5,11,14,17-18:4n3, formed during rumen biohydrogeneration, include novel isomers that are formed through an uncommon isomerisation pattern with distinct double-bond migrations.
rumen biohydrogenesis of stearidionic acid (18:3 n-3) proceeds through an uncommon pathway that involves the formation of conjugates followed by hydrogenation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the biohydrogenated intermediates of 4n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids.
identifying novel biohydrogenated intermediates of 4,7,10,13,16-octadecapentaenoic acid (18:5n-3).
the elucidation of the biohydrogenated products of stearidionic acid in the rumen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the biohydrogenating microorganisms are capable to biohydrogenate 18:4 to 18:0, with the formation of several 18:2 and 18:3 intermediates.
the ruminal biohydrogenation pathway of 18:3n3 and 18:n-3 proceeds via conjugated intermediates and that a novel isomerization pattern is followed by the formation of 18:2n3 and 16:1n7 intermediates.
the biohydrogenating microorganisms in the rumen are capable of producing a wide range of biohydrogenation products, including novel intermediates of 4n-3 fatty acids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
18:4 is biohydrogenated to 18:3, which in turn is hydrogenated to 18 : 2.
the 18:3 intermediates formed by the rumen microorganisms from 18:4 are not the typical Δ5,11 18:3 or Δ9,11 18,3, as found in other studies.
the biohydrogenating pathway of the 4 double-bond containing 18:4 fatty acids seems to be similar to the pathways of the 3 double-bond containing fatty acids, i.e. 18:3n3 and 18:n6.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the biohydrogenated products of 18:3n6 and 18:3 n3 are similar, and the biohydrogenations of these fatty acids are similar to those of 18:2n6.
rumen biohydrogenesis of 18:3n–3 and 18n-4 proceeds through the same pathway with the formation of several novel biohydrogenated intermediates.

the biohydrogenated intermediates of 20:4n-6 and 20:5n-3, which are formed during ruminal biohydrogenation, can also be formed from the 18:3n3 and 18-4n-3 fatty acids, respectively, and therefore the 18:1n-3 and 18n-3 fatty acid biohydrogenation products can serve as a source of these intermediates.
